extracted.intended_audience: researchers preparing systematic or scoping review protocols (health sciences researchers, clinicians, graduate students, librarians)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting a systematic or scoping review protocol (what to include) and how/where to register or publish that protocol. Focused on health-related systematic reviews and practical steps for registration and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for the review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the review is needed. The protocol is your planning document and roadmap for the project: it helps complete the review efficiently and accurately, ensures greater understanding among team members, and makes writing the manuscript far easier. Many journals now require submitted systematic reviews to have registered protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key questions broken into PICO (or other structured research question) components
rubrics_metrics.description: key questions broken into PICO (or other structured research question) components
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the research question(s) using PICO or another appropriate framework so eligibility, search strategy, and synthesis are clear and reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria in the protocol to guide study selection and reduce bias and inconsistency during screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature searches for published/unpublished literature
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify planned search strategies for both published and unpublished (grey) literature, including databases, search terms, limits, and any planned handsearching or contact with authors to capture unpublished studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data abstraction/data management
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how data will be extracted from included studies, what data items will be collected, procedures for data management, storage, and handling of multiple reports or missing data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of methodological quality / risk of bias of individual studies
rubrics_metrics.description: assessment of methodological quality/risk of bias of individual studies (not required for scoping reviews)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which tools and processes will be used to assess study quality/risk of bias for included studies (e.g., which instruments, how many reviewers, resolution processes). Note: this is expected for systematic reviews but is not required for scoping reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data synthesis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe planned methods for synthesizing results (qualitative synthesis, meta-analysis), including how studies will be combined, handling of heterogeneity, subgroup or sensitivity analyses, and criteria for quantitative synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading the evidence for each key question
rubrics_metrics.description: grading the evidence for each key question
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify how the overall strength or certainty of the body of evidence for each key question will be assessed (e.g., GRADE) and how grading will be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PRISMA-P and other guidance/resources when writing the protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: PRISMA for systematic review protocols (PRISMA-P); Practical Guide to Protocol Development; Institute of Medicine standards; Cochrane Handbook; JBI Manual for Evidence Synthesis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standardized guidance and checklists (PRISMA-P checklist and explanation) and established manuals (Cochrane Handbook, IOM Standards, JBI Manual) to ensure the protocol includes required information and follows best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register the protocol with a review registry (PROSPERO or OSF)
rubrics_metrics.description: After you write the protocol, you should register it with a review registry. There are numerous review registries available, such as PROSPERO or OSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is free and open to anyone undertaking systematic reviews. Registering improves transparency and may be required by journals. A PROSPERO record is not considered a full protocol; a PDF of the full protocol may be uploaded as part of the registration record.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROSPERO registration specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: To register a systematic review a member of the review team completes an online registration. They must have signed up for and be logged in to a PROSPERO account. They enter key information about the review design and methods along with information about the review team, funder and timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: PROSPERO is continuing to develop specific forms for different review types; in the meantime all users should select the intervention review form. PROSPERO currently may not accept scoping reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: OSF registration specifics and uses
rubrics_metrics.description: OSF can be used to register a systematic or scoping review protocol and to share documents such as the full protocol, a citation management library, search strategies, and data extraction forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoping reviews may not be registered with PROSPERO but can be registered with the Open Science Framework (OSF). OSF registrations are not editorially reviewed before acceptance. The guide provides an OSF registration form and a Google Doc template to prepare answers; scoping reviews should use the Generalized Systematic Review Template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing a protocol in journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Some journals publish systematic review protocols (e.g., BioMed Central Protocols, BMJ Open, JBI Evidence Synthesis, Systematic Reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies vary: BMC Protocols will consider protocols of any research type following standard peer review; BMJ Open may publish without peer review protocols that have formal ethical approval and funding from a recognized, open-access-advocating research-funding body; other journals follow peer review processes similar to research articles.
